subject: physics
question_text: State the parallelogram law of vectors. Derive an expression for the magnitude and direction of the resultant vector.

verification.note: Question appears in the TSBIE Basic Learning Material 2021-22 (Unit 4) and the Sri Chaitanya IPE Fastrack. The 8-mark split and exact IPE appearance years are claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them.

steps.label: State the law
steps.margin_note: Write the whole statement. The two marks are for the words alone.
lines: If two vectors acting at a point are represented
in magnitude and direction by the two adjacent
sides of a parallelogram drawn from that point,
then their resultant is represented in magnitude
and direction by the diagonal of the parallelogram

recall.must_convey: Both halves of the law: the two vectors at a point are the two adjacent sides of a parallelogram, AND the resultant is the diagonal from that same point. If only one half is spoken, not covered, confidence 0.5 or lower.
accept: two vectors as the two adjacent sides of a parallelogram then the resultant is the diagonal from the same point
if two vectors act at a point they are the sides of a parallelogram and the diagonal is the resultant
adjacent sides represent the two vectors and the diagonal represents the resultant in magnitude and direction
rendu vectors ni parallelogram lo adjacent sides ga theeskunte diagonal ye resultant
first the statement two vectors adjacent sides diagonal is the resultant
reject: the resultant is the sum of the two vectors

steps.label: Draw the figure
steps.margin_note: Label every point: O, A, B, C, D. Mark the angles θ and α and the sides P, Q, R. One mark is for a complete, labelled figure.

recall.must_convey: That a figure is drawn at this point in the answer. Naming the act of drawing is full credit. The student cannot speak a diagram.
accept: then I draw the figure
diagram geestha
draw the parallelogram OACB
I draw a parallelogram with the two vectors as sides
picture veyali
reject: the diagonal of the parallelogram is the resultant

steps.label: Construction
steps.margin_note: Name every point you drew. The examiner matches these names against the figure.
lines: Let OA = P and OB = Q act at the point O,
Join OC. The diagonal OC = R is the resultant.
Draw CD ⊥ to OA extended, meeting it at D.

recall.must_convey: That the construction is written after the figure. Saying the word construction is full credit. So is naming any part of it: OA = P, OB = Q, angle AOB = theta, complete OACB, join OC, drop CD perpendicular to OA extended, angle AOC = alpha.
accept: then construction
OA is P and OB is Q and the angle between them is theta
complete the parallelogram OACB and join OC
drop a perpendicular from C to OA extended
construction raastha

steps.label: Find AD and CD
steps.margin_note: AC is parallel to OB, so the angle at A equals θ. Both legs come from this one triangle.

lines.text: ∴ OD = OA + AD = P + Q cos θ

recall.must_convey: The two legs from right triangle CAD. EITHER naming both legs AD = Q cos theta and CD = Q sin theta, OR naming OD = P + Q cos theta, is enough. Q resolved into a component along P and one perpendicular to P also counts.
accept: AD is Q cos theta and CD is Q sin theta
resolve Q into Q cos theta along OA and Q sin theta perpendicular
OD becomes P plus Q cos theta
in the triangle CAD the angle is theta so the sides are Q cos theta and Q sin theta
components vasthayi Q cos theta and Q sin theta

steps.label: Apply Pythagoras
steps.margin_note: Show the expansion and the sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 step. Skipping it loses the mark.

lines.text: R² = (P + Q cos θ)² + (Q sin θ)²
R² = P² + 2PQ cos θ + Q²cos²θ + Q²sin²θ
R² = P² + Q² + 2PQ cos θ  (∵ sin²θ + cos²θ = 1)

recall.must_convey: EITHER the move (Pythagoras on triangle ODC, OC squared equals OD squared plus CD squared) OR the result (R equals root of P squared plus Q squared plus 2PQ cos theta). Either one alone is full credit.
accept: apply Pythagoras theorem in triangle ODC
OC square equals OD square plus CD square
R equals root of P square plus Q square plus two PQ cos theta
expand it and sin square plus cos square becomes one
pythagoras petti magnitude vasthundi

steps.label: Direction of R
steps.margin_note: Use the same right triangle ODC. Say which side is opposite and which is adjacent to α.
lines: Direction: in the right triangle ODC,

lines.text: tan α = Q sin θ / (P + Q cos θ)

recall.must_convey: The tangent relation for direction: tan alpha = CD / OD, that is tan alpha = Q sin theta over P + Q cos theta. The inverse form spoken at step 7 contains this relation and counts here too.
accept: tan alpha equals CD by OD
tan alpha is Q sin theta over P plus Q cos theta
for the direction tan alpha equals opposite by adjacent
alpha equals tan inverse of Q sin theta by P plus Q cos theta
heard_as: Q sin theta by P plus Q cos theta

steps.label: Final answer for α
steps.margin_note: Box both final answers. The examiner finds them in one glance.
lines: The angle α gives the direction of R with P.

lines.text: ∴ α = tan⁻¹ [ Q sin θ / (P + Q cos θ) ]

recall.must_convey: The final answer written as alpha itself: alpha = tan inverse of [Q sin theta / (P + Q cos theta)]. Saying only tan alpha = ... is step 6, not this step.
accept: alpha equals tan inverse of Q sin theta by P plus Q cos theta
so alpha is tan inverse of that
I box alpha equal to tan inverse
alpha ni tan inverse lo raastha
reject: tan alpha equals Q sin theta by P plus Q cos theta
heard_as: tan to the power minus one

steps.label: Special cases (extra)
steps.margin_note: Not asked. Write it only if time is left.

recall.must_convey: That the special cases are added at the end. Naming them is full credit. Any one of the three values also counts: theta = 0 gives P + Q, theta = 90 gives root P square plus Q square, theta = 180 gives P minus Q.
accept: then special cases
when theta is zero R is P plus Q
at ninety degrees it is root P square plus Q square
maximum when they are in the same direction and minimum when opposite

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.
